s: Deduplicate with ROW_NUMBER on the business key (robust if copies ever differ).
Join the header for dates, customer, channel and region; filter completed orders and the test customer.
Convert to USD per line with the order month's rate; keep the posting month's rate in a second column for Finance.
Name columns for the business and select only what models need.

code.title: vw_FactSales
src: DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_FactSales;
CREATE VIEW vw_FactSales AS
WITH lines AS (
SELECT l.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY l.OrderID, l.LineNo ORDER BY l.OrderID) AS rn
FROM order_lines AS l
SELECT l.OrderID, l.LineNo, o.OrderDate, o.PostingDate, o.CustomerID, o.Channel,
o.SalesRegionKey, l.ProductKey, l.Qty, o.Currency,
ROUND(ROUND(l.Qty * l.UnitPrice * (100 - l.DiscountPct) / 100.0, 2) * COALESCE(fo.USDPerUnit, 1), 2) AS GrossUSD,
ROUND(ROUND(l.Qty * l.UnitPrice * (100 - l.DiscountPct) / 100.0, 2) * COALESCE(fp.USDPerUnit, 1), 2) AS GrossUSDAtPosting
FROM lines AS l
JOIN orders AS o ON o.OrderID = l.OrderID
LEFT JOIN fx_rates AS fo ON fo.Month = SUBSTRING(CAST(o.OrderDate AS VARCHAR(10)), 1, 7)   AND fo.Currency = o.Currency
LEFT JOIN fx_rates AS fp ON fp.Month = SUBSTRING(CAST(o.PostingDate AS VARCHAR(10)), 1, 7) AND fp.Currency = o.Currency
WHERE l.rn = 1 AND o.Status = 'Completed' AND o.CustomerID <> 'C19999';
SELECT COUNT(*) AS Lines, ROUND(SUM(GrossUSD), 2) AS GrossUSD
FROM vw_FactSales
WHERE OrderDate >= '2026-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2026-04-01';

sql-load-0.note: SQL Server: CREATE OR ALTER VIEW instead of DROP/CREATE, and keep the CTE (views can contain CTEs).

s: Read the stored watermark (from a control table, not hard-coded).
Extract rows with OrderDate (better: a LastModified column) greater than the watermark minus the lookback.
Upsert those rows (next assignment), then move the watermark to the maximum value actually loaded, only after the load commits.

code.title: Rows to extract: without and with a 7-day lookback
src: SELECT
(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE OrderDate > '2026-03-24') AS AfterWatermark,
(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE OrderDate > '2026-03-17') AS WithLookback,
(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders)                                AS AllOrders;

s: Reproduce: create an empty table, run the plain INSERT twice, count: the row count doubles.
Fix: insert only keys that aren't there (NOT EXISTS on OrderID + LineNo), or delete the batch first, or MERGE.
Prove: run the fixed load twice and count.

code.title: Idempotent load, run twice
src: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS fact_sales;
CREATE TABLE fact_sales (OrderID VARCHAR(20), LineNo INT, ProductKey INT, Qty INT, UnitPrice DECIMAL(12,2), DiscountPct INT);
-- the load: insert each (OrderID, LineNo) only if it isn't already there
INSERT INTO fact_sales
SELECT s.OrderID, s.LineNo, s.ProductKey, s.Qty, s.UnitPrice, s.DiscountPct
FROM (SELECT l.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY OrderID, LineNo ORDER BY OrderID) AS rn FROM order_lines AS l) AS s
WHERE s.rn = 1
AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fact_sales AS f WHERE f.OrderID = s.OrderID AND f.LineNo = s.LineNo);
-- the re-run after a failure: exactly the same statement
INSERT INTO fact_sales
SELECT s.OrderID, s.LineNo, s.ProductKey, s.Qty, s.UnitPrice, s.DiscountPct
FROM (SELECT l.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY OrderID, LineNo ORDER BY OrderID) AS rn FROM order_lines AS l) AS s
WHERE s.rn = 1
AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fact_sales AS f WHERE f.OrderID = s.OrderID AND f.LineNo = s.LineNo);
SELECT COUNT(*) AS RowsAfterTwoRuns FROM fact_sales;

code.title: The same with MERGE (SQL Server)
src: MERGE dbo.FactSales AS f
USING stage.OrderLines AS s
ON f.OrderID = s.OrderID AND f.LineNo = s.LineNo
WHEN MATCHED AND (f.Qty <> s.Qty OR f.UnitPrice <> s.UnitPrice OR f.DiscountPct <> s.DiscountPct)
THEN UPDATE SET Qty = s.Qty, UnitPrice = s.UnitPrice, DiscountPct = s.DiscountPct
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET
THEN INSERT (OrderID, LineNo, ProductKey, Qty, UnitPrice, DiscountPct)
VALUES (s.OrderID, s.LineNo, s.ProductKey, s.Qty, s.UnitPrice, s.DiscountPct);

sql-load-2.check: Two runs → {{sql_distinct_rows|int}} rows, the same as one run.
sql-load-2.note: Also add a unique constraint on (OrderID, LineNo) in the warehouse: then a bad load fails loudly instead of silently duplicating.
